applicable_when: R0_BLOCK=512 is 4x larger than the actual reduction dimension (r0_numel=128). Triton allocates accumulator arrays of shape [XBLOCK, R0_BLOCK] = [128, 512] = 65536 elements per block. This far exceeds available registers (128 threads x 32 regs = 4096 register slots), forcing massive register spilling to local memory. The spilled accesses are strided (one element per thread across 32-byte sectors), explaining the catastrophic 1/32 byte utilization. This causes 91% of scheduler cycles to stall on L1TEX scoreboard waits. The fix is to set R0_BLOCK=128 (matching r0_numel exactly), eliminating the spill entirely. Additionally, adding @triton.autotune explores XBLOCK and num_warps to recover occupancy.

strategy_title: Fuse Two-Pass Softmax Into Single Register-Resident Pass
strategy_description: When a reduction kernel performs two sequential passes over the same global memory data (pass-1 accumulates online softmax max/sum; pass-2 re-reads the same data to compute exp/normalize/output), and the reduction dimension fits entirely within one tile (R0_BLOCK == r0_numel), the second pass can be eliminated by computing the output inline at the end of the first pass using still-live register values. This directly eliminates the dominant stall source: L1TEX scoreboard waits caused by re-fetching data evicted between passes (L1 hit rate 3.39% → 24.39%, warp cycles per instruction 34.37 → 4.43). The fix also reduces shared memory usage per block (65 KB → 33 KB), which relaxes the shared-memory block limit and allows more waves per SM (42 → 63), while compute throughput rises from 11.89% to 44.4% of peak.
slow_pseudocode:
# Pass 1: accumulate online softmax state
for r0_offset in range(0, r0_numel, R0_BLOCK):  # R0_BLOCK=512 >> r0_numel=128
    tmp0 = load(in_ptr0[r0, x])   # global load
    tmp1 = load(in_ptr1[r0])      # global load
    tmp2 = tmp0 + tmp1
    _max, _sum = online_softmax_combine(_max, _sum, tmp2)

tmp4, tmp5 = online_softmax_reduce(_max, _sum)  # cross-warp reduce

# Pass 2: re-read same data, compute output
for r0_offset in range(0, r0_numel, R0_BLOCK):
    tmp6 = load(in_ptr0[r0, x])   # REDUNDANT global load
    tmp7 = load(in_ptr1[r0])      # REDUNDANT global load
    tmp12 = load(in_ptr2[r0])
    out = sigmoid((softmax(tmp6+tmp7, tmp4, tmp5) + tmp12) * 2.0)
    store(out_ptr[...])
fast_pseudocode:
# SINGLE PASS: load all inputs once, accumulate state, compute output inline
# Requires R0_BLOCK == r0_numel so loop body executes exactly once
for r0_offset in range(0, r0_numel, R0_BLOCK):  # R0_BLOCK=128 == r0_numel
    tmp0 = load(in_ptr0[r0, x])   # loaded once
    tmp1 = load(in_ptr1[r0])      # loaded once
    tmp12 = load(in_ptr2[r0])     # loaded once
    tmp2 = tmp0 + tmp1
    _max, _sum = online_softmax_combine(_max, _sum, tmp2)
    # Values still live in registers — compute output immediately
    tmp4_g, tmp5_g = online_softmax_reduce(_max, _sum)
    out = sigmoid((softmax(tmp2, tmp4_g, tmp5_g) + tmp12) * 2.0)
    store(out_ptr[...])

# Also: set R0_BLOCK=r0_numel (128) instead of oversized 512
# Use @triton.autotune for XBLOCK and num_warps
applicable_when: Triton reduction kernel with two sequential tl.range loops over the same global memory (two-pass softmax pattern); L1TEX hit rate < 10% indicating data evicted between passes; CPIStall rule triggered with L1TEX scoreboard stalls > 50% of stall budget; reduction dimension (r0_numel) is small enough to fit in one tile (R0_BLOCK can equal r0_numel); R0_BLOCK is set larger than r0_numel (wasted iterations).
do_not_apply_when: r0_numel is too large to fit in a single tile (loop must execute multiple times, so values are not all live in registers simultaneously); the two passes have data dependencies that prevent fusion (e.g., pass-2 requires a fully-reduced global value that cannot be computed per-tile); occupancy is already register-limited and adding more register pressure (255 registers/thread) would cause spilling or further reduce occupancy below a useful threshold.
framework_notes: Triton-specific: set R0_BLOCK as a tl.constexpr equal to r0_numel so the compiler can fully unroll the loop. Use @triton.autotune to explore XBLOCK and num_warps configs since the optimal block shape changes after fusion. The inline reduce (online_softmax_reduce inside the loop) is valid only when R0_BLOCK == r0_numel so the partial state equals the full state after one iteration. In CUDA, the equivalent is fusing two kernel passes into one kernel with shared-memory reduction, keeping loaded values in registers across the reduction.
